title: Rank-zero vector-bundle operators lower coherent support dimension
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $Z$ a Noetherian finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where Noetherian includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose $\dim Z\leq d$ for an integer $d\geq0$, using Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] on affine charts. Let $G_0(Z)$ be the abelian group generated by coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] modulo short exact sequence relations. For $-1\leq k\leq d$, let $F_kG_0(Z)$ be the subgroup generated by modules whose closed support has dimension at most $k$, with $F_{-1}=0$. Then $F_d=G_0(Z)$. Every locally finite free $\mathcal O_Z$-module $E$ of constant finite rank $n$ defines an endomorphism $T_E[\mathcal M]=[E\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}\mathcal M]$, and
$$(T_E-n\,\mathrm{id})(F_kG_0(Z))\subseteq F_{k-1}G_0(Z)\qquad(0\leq k\leq d).$$
For any commutative ring $B$, put $H=G_0(Z)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B$ and let $F_kH$ be the image of $F_kG_0(Z)\otimes B$. The scalar-extended operators have the same lowering property. Consequently any finite $B$-linear combination $D$ of operators $T_{E_j}-\operatorname{rank}(E_j)\,\mathrm{id}$ satisfies $D^{d+1}=0$ on $H$. No regularity of $Z$, rational coefficients, or assumption that $G_0(Z)$ is torsion-free is imposed.

source.place: Tags 02S8 (lemma-Serre-subcategories), 02S9 (lemma-cycles-k-group), and homology.tex Tag 02MX (lemma-serre-subcategory-K-groups). Agent-formulated tensor-rank consequence of the dimension-support filtration; 02S9 identifies its graded quotient with cycles using generic lengths.

proof.text: A coherent module $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], since $Z$ is locally Noetherian. Its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. A chain of irreducible closed subsets of this support is also such a chain in $Z$, so its dimension is at most $d$. Thus every generator of $G_0(Z)$ belongs to $F_d$ and $F_d=G_0(Z)$. The only sheaf with empty support is zero: a section with zero germ at every point is locally zero and hence zero by the sheaf axiom. This agrees with $F_{-1}=0$.

source.place: Dimension-support filtration in the paragraph before Tag 02S8; coherence and closed support as cited.

proof.text: Choose local frames $E|_U\simeq\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$. Tensoring gives $(E\otimes\mathcal M)|_U\simeq(\mathcal M|_U)^{\oplus n}$: the forward map sends $(a_i)_i\otimes m$ to $(a_i m)_i$, and its inverse sends $(m_i)_i$ to $\sum_i e_i\otimes m_i$. These inverse balanced maps commute with restrictions and so define inverse sheaf maps. Finite sums of coherent modules are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum]; coherence is local by the finite-generator and finite-type-kernel conditions in [pqf-def-coherent]. Hence $E\otimes\mathcal M$ is coherent. At any point outside $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal M$ the local displayed sum has zero stalk, so tensoring does not increase support. By [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact] tensoring preserves short exact sequences. Therefore it respects every defining relation and yields $T_E$ on $G_0(Z)$ and on each $K_0(\mathcal C_k(Z))$.

source.place: Agent tensor calculation supporting the use of the support categories of 02S8 and 02S9.

proof.text: Fix $0\leq k\leq d$ and $\mathcal M\in\mathcal C_k(Z)$. Apply [lem-sfb-coherent-support-cycle-exact-sequence] to obtain the finite generic lengths defining $c_k$. At each $\eta_V$ appearing there, a frame near that point identifies $(E\otimes\mathcal M)_{\eta_V}$ with $\mathcal M_{\eta_V}^{\oplus n}$ as modules over the same local ring. The split exact sequence $0\to L^{\oplus r}\to L^{\oplus(r+1)}\to L\to0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] give $\operatorname{length}(L^{\oplus n})=n\operatorname{length}(L)$ by induction from $n=0$. Thus every coefficient of $c_k([E\otimes\mathcal M]-n[\mathcal M])$ is zero. Exactness of the cited cycle sequence supplies an element $y\in K_0(\mathcal C_{k-1}(Z))$ whose inclusion is this difference. Mapping the equality to $G_0(Z)$ shows $(T_E-n\,\mathrm{id})[\mathcal M]\in F_{k-1}$. Since such $[\mathcal M]$ generate $F_k$, this proves the lowering property, also for $k=0$ since $K_0(\mathcal C_{-1})=0$.

source.place: Tags 02S9 and 02MX(1), followed by the agent generic-stalk tensor-rank calculation.

proof.text: Write $A_E=T_E-n\,\mathrm{id}$. On $H$, its scalar extension is defined on pure tensors by $\overline A_E(x\otimes b)=A_E(x)\otimes b$; additivity and the integer balancing relation make it well defined and $B$-linear. An element of $F_kH$ is a finite sum $\sum_i x_i\otimes b_i$ with $x_i\in F_kG_0(Z)$. Step 3 puts its image in $F_{k-1}H$. This argument uses images of tensors and does not require the inclusions $F_kG_0\to G_0$ to stay injective after tensoring. Step 1 gives $F_dH=H$ and $F_{-1}H=0$.

source.place: Agent scalar-extension calculation after the integral filtration argument.

proof.text: Let $D=\sum_{j=1}^s b_j\overline A_{E_j}$ with $b_j\in B$. Each summand sends $F_kH$ into $F_{k-1}H$ by step 4, and $F_{k-1}H$ is a $B$-submodule by its definition as an image. Hence $D$ lowers the same filtration. Induction on $r$ gives $D^r(H)\subseteq F_{d-r}H$ for $0\leq r\leq d+1$, starting with $D^0(H)=H=F_dH$ and applying the lowering inclusion at each step. At $r=d+1$ this is $D^{d+1}(H)\subseteq F_{-1}H=0$. No commutation of distinct tensor operators is needed. Empty sums, rank zero, the zero ring $B$, $Z=\varnothing$ and $d=0$ are all included in these formulas.
